title: 74. The Six Wives of Henry VIII

sentences.en: O death, rock me asleep, bring me the quiet reSt.
sentences.zh: 啊，死神，让我安眠，带给我宁静的休憩。

sentences.en: Let pass my weary, guiltless ghost out of my careful breaSt.
sentences.zh: 让疲惫而无辜的灵魂从我焦虑的胸膛中离去。

sentences.en: These lines are attributed to Anne Boleyn.
sentences.zh: 这些诗句据说是安妮·博林所作。

sentences.en: She supposedly wrote them in 1536 in the Tower of London as she was awaiting execution at the hands of a French swordsman who had been brought over specially for the purpose
sentences.zh: 据称她在1536年被关押在伦敦塔时写下了这些，当时她正等待着被处决，行刑者是一名特地请来的法国剑手，

sentences.en: by her erstwhile husband, King Henry VIII, whose marital history has inspired another poem,
sentences.zh: 受她曾经的丈夫亨利八世之命。亨利的婚姻史催生了另一首诗，

sentences.en: Divorced, Beheaded, Died, Divorced, Beheaded, Survived.
sentences.zh: 离婚、斩首、死亡，离婚、斩首、幸存。

sentences.en: And Dominic Sambra with me.
sentences.zh: 还有多米尼克·桑布拉和我。

sentences.en: Probably the most famously disastrous sequence of marriages in English history.
sentences.zh: 这大概是英国历史上最著名的灾难性婚姻连续剧。

sentences.en: In English history, in world history.
sentences.zh: 在英国历史上，在世界历史上。

sentences.en: Probably the whole of history.
sentences.zh: 大概是整部人类历史上。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's an irresistible subject, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 对啊，这是一个让人无法抗拒的主题，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it's the stuff of soap operas, it's the stuff of costume dramas,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是肥皂剧的素材，这就是古装剧的素材，

sentences.en: it's the stuff of about a thousand Channel 5 documentaries.
sentences.zh: 这也是大约一千部第五频道纪录片的素材。

sentences.en: Well, it's amazing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这太神奇了。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, we're well into the 70s, I think.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道的，我们已经做到70多集了，我想。

sentences.en: We've done over 70 episodes.
sentences.zh: 我们已经做了70多集节目了。

sentences.en: It's kind of extraordinary that we haven't really done one before.
sentences.zh: 真有点不可思议，我们以前竟然一直没做过这个。

sentences.en: Yeah, we've shown Herculean self-restraint, I think.
sentences.zh: 对，我觉得我们展现出了海格力斯般的自制力。

sentences.en: I guess if we were, you know, if we were a TV company, we'd have done six already.
sentences.zh: 我想如果我们是，你知道的，如果我们是一家电视台，我们大概已经拍了六季了。

sentences.en: If we would.
sentences.zh: 如果我们会的话。

sentences.en: Actually, the reason why we have delayed it, doing The Six Wives of Henry VIII,
sentences.zh: 其实，我们之所以推迟做《亨利八世的六个王后》这个主题，

sentences.en: obviously there have been many, many great scholars over the years who have written about the reign of Henry VIII.
sentences.zh: 很显然，多年来有许许多多伟大的学者写过关于亨利八世统治时期的著作。

sentences.en: One thinks of Sir Geoffrey Elton, J.G.
sentences.zh: 人们会想到杰弗里·埃尔顿爵士、J·G·

sentences.en: Scarrisbrick, David Starkey.
sentences.zh: 斯卡里斯布里克、大卫·斯塔基。

sentences.en: But these scholars have now been joined by a new kid on the block, Dominic Sandbrook.
sentences.zh: 但这些学者现在迎来了体坛新秀般的后辈，多米尼克·桑德布鲁克。

sentences.en: Dominic, your book, The Six Wives of Henry VIII.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你的书《亨利八世的六个王后》。

sentences.en: Tom, I don't like the slightly ironic way in which you're, you know.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我不太喜欢你那种带点讽刺意味的语气，你知道的。

sentences.en: No, but to explain, this is written for children.
sentences.zh: 不，但解释一下，这是为孩子们写的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And absolutely fabulous.
sentences.zh: 而且绝对精彩。

sentences.en: I read it last night, and I'm not in any way just saying that.
sentences.zh: 我昨晚读了，我绝不仅仅是在客套。

sentences.en: I hugely enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 我看得非常过瘾。

sentences.en: And I guess, so your other book is on the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 我想，你的另一本书是关于第二次世界大战的。

sentences.en: Henry VIII and the Second World War, those are the two big topics.
sentences.zh: 亨利八世和第二次世界大战，这是两个重大主题。

sentences.en: But Henry VIII, really, I mean, it's a timeless classic, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但亨利八世，说真的，这是一个永恒的经典，不是吗？

sentences.en: It is, and actually, I was always a bit suspicious of it.
sentences.zh: 确实是，其实我以前对它一直有点怀疑。

sentences.en: I was never a great aficionado of the Tudors or of The Six Wives of Henry VIII.
sentences.zh: 我从来都不是都铎王朝或亨利八世六个王后的超级狂热粉。

sentences.en: I always slightly bridled at the sort of, oh, I don't know, the sort of soap opera-y nature of it.
sentences.zh: 我总是对那种，哦，我不知道，那种肥皂剧般的性质有点本能的抵触。

sentences.en: But then when I started getting into it, I actually found it irresistible.
sentences.zh: 但当我真正开始深入了解时，我发现它确实让人欲罢不能。

sentences.en: And it's partly the court politics and the sort of Game of Thrones style kind of bed-hopping shenanigans and all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于宫廷政治，以及那种《权力的游戏》风格的频繁换床伴的勾当之类的事情。

sentences.en: But the fact is, it happens at an absolute hinge moment of history, and against the backdrop of these colossal religious changes, which mean that this is, without question,
sentences.zh: 但事实是，它发生在历史的一个绝对转折点上，并以这些巨大的宗教变革为背景，这意味着毫无疑问，

sentences.en: the biggest political and cultural break in England's history.
sentences.zh: 这是英国历史上最大的一次政治和文化断裂。

sentences.en: And it's all snarled up with Anne Boleyn's sex appeal.
sentences.zh: 而这一切都和安妮·博林的性吸引力纠缠在一起。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Henry's luSt.
sentences.zh: 亨利的色欲。

sentences.en: So the weird thing is that all these things that it's very easy to dismiss as froth and gossip and the stuff of kind of some Tudor tattler, they really matter.
sentences.zh: 所以奇怪的是，所有这些很容易被当作泡沫、八卦和都铎王朝八卦小报素材的东西，其实都至关重要。

sentences.en: They change the lives of millions of people.
sentences.zh: 它们改变了数百万人的生活。

sentences.en: And that's what makes it so enduringly fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这就是它历久弥新、令人着迷的原因。

sentences.en: Well, I remember the first time I went to the Loire, I must have been, I don't know, 20 or something,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我记得我第一次去卢瓦尔河谷的时候，我大概，我不知道，20岁左右吧，

sentences.en: and visiting all these kind of incredible chateaus that had been built by Henry VIII's exact contemporary, François Premier, Francis I of France, who was king of, you know,
sentences.zh: 参观了所有这些不可思议的城堡，它们是由亨利八世的同时代人弗朗索瓦一世建造的，也就是法国国王弗朗西斯一世，他是，你知道的，

sentences.en: a much more, much richer, in many ways, much more sophisticated country than England.
sentences.zh: 在一个各方面都比英国大得多、也富裕得多、在很多方面也更成熟的国家。

sentences.en: And I felt kind of quite intimidated, looking at these glories to Gaelic civilisation.
sentences.zh: 看着这些盖尔文明的荣耀，我感到相当敬畏。

sentences.en: But then I thought, yeah, but how many wives did Francis I have?
sentences.zh: 但后来我想，对啊，可是弗朗西斯一世有几个老婆？

sentences.en: Henry VIII is a much, much better character.
sentences.zh: 亨利八世是一个好得多、丰满得多的角色。

sentences.en: And I felt a kind of patriotic glow.
sentences.zh: 我心中涌起了一种爱国主义的暖意。

sentences.en: Oh, that's good to hear.
sentences.zh: 哦，很高兴听到这个。

sentences.en: That's very good to hear.
sentences.zh: 听到这个真好。

sentences.en: Well, Francis I, I mean, Henry did measure himself against Francis I of France.
sentences.zh: 嗯，弗朗西斯一世，我是说，亨利确实拿自己跟法国的弗朗西斯一世作比较。

sentences.en: And he also measured himself against, so there are basically three big kings, aren't there, at this point?
sentences.zh: 而且他也拿自己跟——所以此时基本上有三个大国王，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, there are two big kings, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 嗯，有两个大国王，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, there are two big kings in one kind of, kind of, kind of trying to join the club.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有两个大国王，还有一个在某种程度上，某种程度上，某种程度上试图加入这个俱乐部。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So there's Francis, or François, and then there's Charles, or Carlos V of Spain, who is also the ruler of the Holy Roman Empire, is just unbelievably rich,
sentences.zh: 所以有弗朗西斯，或者说弗朗索瓦，然后有查理，也就是西班牙的卡洛斯五世，他同时也是神圣罗马帝国的统治者，简直富得流油，

sentences.en: and has this massive dominion.
sentences.zh: 并且拥有庞大的领地。

sentences.en: You know, he's got South America, and he's, I mean, he is by far the most potent monarch of the day.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他拥有南美洲，而且，我的意思是，他是当今无可争议的最强君主。

sentences.en: And poor old Henry, you know, he just rules England, and he's desperate.
sentences.zh: 而可怜的亨利，你知道的，他只统治英格兰，他非常渴望。

sentences.en: He's absolutely desperate to be taken seriously by these two guys.
sentences.zh: 他极度渴望被这两个家伙认真对待。

sentences.en: And he never, and he's changing his wives all the time.
sentences.zh: 但他从来没有，而且他一直在换老婆。

sentences.en: And there's this sort of farcical, comical element to him, as well as the sort of terrifying and more sinister element.
sentences.zh: 除了那种可怕和更加阴暗的成分之外，他身上也有一种荒诞滑稽的元素。

sentences.en: Well, he, yeah, I mean, I think he only seems comical if he does seem comical.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他，对，我是说，我觉得他只有在看起来滑稽的时候才显得滑稽。

sentences.en: And, of course, he was played by Sid James in the Carry On film, so I guess there is a slight element of the comic.
sentences.zh: 当然，他在《滑稽》系列电影里由西德·詹姆斯扮演，所以我想确实有一点喜剧色彩。

sentences.en: But up close, I mean, he's a very frightening figure.
sentences.zh: 但近距离来看，我的意思是，他是一个非常可怕的人物。

sentences.en: And the fact that he is actually able to go toe-to-toe with the great kings on the continent, I think,
sentences.zh: 事实上，他居然能够与欧洲大陆的大国君主们分庭抗礼，我认为，

sentences.en: are a kind of measure of the swagger and the power and the charisma that he does have.
sentences.zh: 这正是他所具有的傲气、权力和个人魅力的某种体现。

sentences.en: And that even non-English people experience.
sentences.zh: 甚至连非英国人也能感受到这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, he's a very, very intimidating.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他非常、非常具有震慑力。

sentences.en: But you don't get Henry right, I think, unless you emphasise exactly what you just said about his charisma.
sentences.zh: 但如果你不强调你刚才所说的他的个人魅力，你就无法真正理解亨利。

sentences.en: So when he becomes king, I mean, he's a very impressive person.
sentences.zh: 所以当他成为国王时，我的意思是，他是一个非常令人印象深刻的人。

sentences.en: He plays tennis.
sentences.zh: 他打网球。

sentences.en: He writes music.
sentences.zh: 他谱曲。

sentences.en: He writes songs.
sentences.zh: 他写歌。

sentences.en: He speaks lots of languages.
sentences.zh: 他说很多种语言。

sentences.en: He's physically impressive, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他在体格上就很震撼人，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, he's very, very tall.
sentences.zh: 对，他非常、非常高大。

sentences.en: He's very good-looking.
sentences.zh: 他长得很帅。

sentences.en: He's very muscular, very large.
sentences.zh: 他非常强壮，体型魁梧。

sentences.en: Handsome.
sentences.zh: 英俊。

sentences.en: I mean, everybody says he's handsome.
sentences.zh: 我是说，所有人都说他很英俊。

sentences.en: He looks like a king.
sentences.zh: 他看起来就像个国王。

sentences.en: And he actually behaves.
sentences.zh: 而且他的行为举止。

sentences.en: He plays the part of a king very well.
sentences.zh: 他把国王的角色演得很好。

sentences.en: I mean, that's one thing I think that sometimes people forget, is that actually to people at the time, what strikes them is not, oh,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是人们有时会忘记的一点，那就是实际上对于当时的人们来说，打动他们的并不是，哦，

sentences.en: he's a complete monster and he's so fat and all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他是个彻头彻尾的怪物，他怎么这么胖之类的。

sentences.en: What strikes them is he looks and behaves exactly as a king should.
sentences.zh: 打动他们的是，他的外表和举止完全符合一个国王应有的样子。

sentences.en: And if he is sometimes cruel and capricious, I think to a lot of people in the 16th century, those things were sort of perhaps slightly lamentable.
sentences.zh: 如果他有时残酷而反复无常，我想对于16世纪的许多人来说，这些事情可能稍微有些令人惋惜。

sentences.en: But they were better than being weak and dithery and pious and sort of a bit sanctimonious and waffly, like Henry VI, for example,
sentences.zh: 但它们总比软弱、优柔寡断、笃信宗教且有点假惺惺、吞吞吐吐要好，比如亨利六世，

sentences.en: or was praying when he should have been killing people.
sentences.zh: 或者本该杀伐决断时却在祈祷的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They like a strong ruler.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢强有力的统治者。

sentences.en: And the context for Henry's reign is exactly the Wars of the Roses, where Henry VI of Lancaster is so useless that he ends up kind of being deposed twice, basically.
sentences.zh: 亨利统治时期的背景正是玫瑰战争，当时兰开斯特家族的亨利六世昏庸无能，以至于最后基本上被废黜了两次。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: By one of, yeah.
sentences.zh: 被其中一个，对。

sentences.en: And then you've got, well, actually, you begin your book with Bosworth, don't you?
sentences.zh: 然后你有了，嗯，实际上，你的书是从博斯沃思战役开始的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, because I think that's really important to understand his context so that he, first of all, he doesn't know he's early modern rather than late medieval.
sentences.zh: 对，因为我认为这对于理解他的背景非常重要，首先，他并不觉得自己属于近代早期而不是中世纪晚期。

sentences.en: You know, he, at the back of his mind are the Wars of the Roses.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他脑海深处盘桓的是玫瑰战争。

sentences.en: And secondly, he doesn't know that the Wars of the Roses are over.
sentences.zh: 其次，他并不知道玫瑰战争已经结束了。

sentences.en: So we conventionally think, say, well, they ended in 1485 when his father, a Tudor, you know, Welsh adventurer from a little branch of the family,
sentences.zh: 所以我们习惯上认为，嗯，它们在1485年结束了，当时他的父亲，一个都铎家族的人，你知道的，来自家族一个分支的威尔士冒险家，

sentences.en: basically is the last man standing after this great Game of Thrones style bloodbath.
sentences.zh: 在经历了一场《权力的游戏》风格的大屠杀后，基本上成了最后站着的人。

sentences.en: But Henry VIII doesn't know that that's all over.
sentences.zh: 但亨利八世并不知道这一切都结束了。

sentences.en: I mean, neither of the two Henry's do.
sentences.zh: 我是说，两个亨利都不知道。

sentences.en: For them, they think there could be a revolt at any moment, that the old kind of guard, the old nobility could be plotting against them, which actually, frankly,
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，他们觉得随时可能发生叛乱，旧的卫队、旧的贵族可能在密谋反对他们，而实际上坦白说，

sentences.en: a lot of the time they are.
sentences.zh: 他们很多时候确实在密谋。

sentences.en: So there's that sort of insecurity and that fear.
sentences.zh: 所以存在那种不安全感和恐惧。

sentences.en: And that lies behind this whole business of the son.
sentences.zh: 而这正是所有关于生儿子这件事的根源。

sentences.en: He has to have an heir because he knows if I don't have an heir, then basically everything my dad and I have done will be for nothing.
sentences.zh: 他必须有个继承人，因为他知道如果我没有继承人，那么我和我父亲所做的一切基本上都将化为乌有。

sentences.en: And those bastards will get the throne back again.
sentences.zh: 而那些混蛋会重新夺回王位。

sentences.en: And that's at the back of his mind the whole time.
sentences.zh: 这在他的脑海里挥之不去。

sentences.en: That fear, you know, that people, these, this stuff about him being paranoid, which you often read.
sentences.zh: 那种恐惧，你知道的，人们，这些关于他偏执的说法，你经常能读到。

sentences.en: Oh, Henry was paranoid.
sentences.zh: 哦，亨利太偏执了。

sentences.en: He was like Stalin or whatever.
sentences.zh: 他就像斯大林或者别的什么人。

sentences.en: I mean, he's only paranoid in the sense that he takes it a little bit further than you or I might have done.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他只是在比你我可能做到的程度更进一步的意义上才显得偏执。

sentences.en: But frankly, he lives at a time when if you don't kill people first, they probably will kill you.
sentences.zh: 但说实话，他生活在一个如果你不先杀别人，别人很可能会杀你的时代。

sentences.en: Although, I mean, fair enough.
sentences.zh: 尽管，我的意思是，这也算情有可原。

sentences.en: But if you're marrying him, I mean, it's definitely a consideration to bear in mind, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但如果你要嫁给他，这绝对是一个需要考虑的因素，不是吗？

sentences.en: And also, I suppose the other consideration to bear in mind as he gets older is that he gets fatter and fatter and less attractive.
sentences.zh: 而且我想，随着他年龄增长，另一个需要考虑的因素是，他变得越来越胖，越来越没有吸引力。

sentences.en: And he starts to get smelly, pus-ridden ulcers all up his legs.
sentences.zh: 他的双腿开始长出散发恶臭、流脓的溃疡。

sentences.en: And ultimately, he ends up so fat, does he not, Dominic, that he has to have enemas.
sentences.zh: 最后，他胖到不行，不是吗，多米尼克，以至于他必须接受灌肠。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The enemas are rare.
sentences.zh: 灌肠是很罕见的。

sentences.en: Which you may conceivably mention in your book.
sentences.zh: 你可能在书里顺便提到了这一点。

sentences.en: I know you love this detail about the enemas.
sentences.zh: 我知道你很喜欢关于灌肠的这个细节。

sentences.en: Basically, anyone who ever encounters my book thinks this is either the best thing or the least worst thing in it,
sentences.zh: 基本上，任何读过我书的人都认为这是书中最好的一点，或者是没那么糟的一点，

sentences.en: which is this description of how Homer's doctors would push this greased tube up his bottom, which was then attached to it.
sentences.zh: 也就是对霍默的医生如何将这根涂了油的管子塞进他屁股的描写，管子还连着。

sentences.en: I think it's kind of a metal tube.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那是一种金属管。

sentences.en: And it's attached to a pig's bladder that's filled with honey and milk and herbs and stuff.
sentences.zh: 它连着一个装满了蜂蜜、牛奶和草药之类东西的猪膀胱。

sentences.en: And they squirt this.
sentences.zh: 然后他们把这些喷射进去。
